subject: 7F0EB703B6D6E3DF376EE1FB68894FF6
introduction: These prayers are said by, or for, someone about to teach: a traveller setting out, a speaker before a meeting, a believer who feels like “a broken-winged bird”. They confess incapacity and ask for speech, for wisdom, for courage, and for hearers able to hear. Moses and Jeremiah made the same confession and received the same promise; the first Christians prayed for “all boldness”; Paul asked others to pray that “utterance may be given” him; and the Qur’an’s rule, “with wisdom and fair exhortation”, is the manner these prayers ask for.
questions: Why do the prayers begin from weakness? What would be wrong with a confident teacher’s prayer?
Reading 6 prays for the hearers. What can a teacher not do for them?
Is it eloquence that these prayers want, or something eloquence serves?

outside.why: In lowliness and weakness, occupied with the greatest undertaking. O my Lord, I am not eloquent; I am slow of speech. And the Lord said, I will be with thy mouth.
We are sightless, make us seeing. He giveth power to the faint; they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles.
A broken-winged bird whose flight is slow. Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.
Walking in Thy dominion to exalt Thy Word. Paul asked his friends to pray that utterance may be given unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly.
Grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word.
Assist the hearers. Other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit: the parable is about hearing.
Aid this servant to spread the fragrances. I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.
Standing before the throne, hearing Thy call. Here am I; send me.
By the Word through which all things spoke. The Lord God hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary.
That He increase thy speech and joy. Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation.
Trusting in God despite weakness. The kingdom of God is not in word, but in power. These prayers ask for eloquence. What else, on their own showing, does a teacher need more?

shortfall: The later prayers repeat the first eleven for other teachers; companions were set to those.
